question.text: During due diligence on Lakshmi AIF Partners, an investor is reviewing competing or outside interests of the investment manager. Why is this an important area to check?

answer.text: Other fund or business obligations may compromise the manager's time, devotion, or deal-flow allocation to this AIF
It tells the investor whether the manager has invested personal funds in any asset class
It indicates whether the manager holds any directorship in any company
It reveals which industry conferences the manager attends each year

explanation.text: The Logic: A manager handling several funds, other AIF interests, or other business obligations may not be able to devote sufficient time and attention to this AIF, and competing mandates can affect how investment opportunities and deal flow are allocated. Reviewing these outside interests during due diligence helps an investor assess potential conflicts. The Trap: Personal investments and directorships sound relevant but are far broader than what the workbook describes; the focus is specifically on competing or outside professional interests that affect time, devotion, and deal referral to this AIF. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 168-169, which list competing or outside interests of the manager as a due-diligence area because of their impact on time, devotion, and deal referral.
